title: Payment Retry Queue
summary: Use a queue to retry failed payments in the order they arrived.

dsa.title: Queue
dsa.angle: FIFO structure, enqueue, dequeue, peek, and empty state.
dsa.studentTakeaway: The first item added is the first item removed.

system_design.title: Retry Pipeline
system_design.angle: A payment retry queue protects workers from bursts and keeps failed payments ordered.
system_design.studentTakeaway: Queues help systems handle work at a safe pace.

game_theory.title: Congestion and Fairness
game_theory.angle: Selfish producers can overload shared workers unless the queue has fair ordering and backpressure.
game_theory.studentTakeaway: Fair ordering changes how users and services compete for limited processing.

story.context: A payment service needs to retry failed charges without losing order or flooding the worker.
story.goal: Understand why FIFO order matters before writing the queue.

python.tests:
q = PaymentRetryQueue()
assert_equal(q.is_empty(), True, 'new queue starts empty')
q.enqueue('pay_101')
q.enqueue('pay_102')
assert_equal(q.peek(), 'pay_101', 'peek returns front item')
assert_equal(q.dequeue(), 'pay_101', 'dequeue returns first item')
assert_equal(q.dequeue(), 'pay_102', 'dequeue returns second item')
assert_equal(q.is_empty(), True, 'queue is empty after removing all items')
